newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains,seen inching up or flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains,seen inching up or flat.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday extended Tuesday's gains in higher turnover and analysts were divided on whether the market would be able to achieve modest growth or continue its six-week sideways trend.
Some analysts said the higher turnovers over two days of growth signalled that the market, currently at 13,818.6 points, could test resistance at 14,000 before the end of the year.

Others said the stronger selling after price fixing in part reflected pessimism after the central bank president said interest rates might rise if fast credit growth continues, and the news the country's current account gap was widening.

"I think the stronger selling after price fixing was a one-day delayed reaction to the current account deficit information and (Hanna) Gronkiewicz-Waltz's statement of a possible or necessary rate rise," said Wojciech Bialek, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.7 percent to 13,818.6 points and turnover rose 21.9 percent to 108.2 million zlotys ($37.9 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 46 to 16 with 21 stocks.
Analysts said investors would be watching firms' November earnings results, the bulk of which are being released after Wednesday's session.

Analysts said top gainer bank BWR, up 4.3 percent in moderate trade, may have been helped by the news it would buy back shares on the bourse to take over Bank Secesyjny SA rather than issue new shares.
Continuous trade turnover was at five million zlotys ($1.8 million) with two stocks up, two down and five flat.
Mass privatisation NFI units eased 0.4 percent to 138 zlotys ($48.3) in the regular session and fell 1.4 percent to 137 zlotys ($48) in 5.3-million-zloty ($1.9 million) continuous trade.
